explainedBy: Toru reads quietly in his dorm room, reflecting how literature conditions people to expect narrative logic from trauma.

storyboard.claim: Literature and film condition people to expect trauma to follow neat narrative logic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits alone in his spartan dorm room reading a book, searching literature for order.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from Kizuki's suicide in the garage to the host's commentary on narrative expectations.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the hosts' abstract observation about fiction directly in Toru's private reading.

explainedBy: Toru sits with his book, contrasting the grand reasons promised in fiction with Kizuki's total silence.

storyboard.claim: People expect an elaborate explanation, a final letter, or a grand reason when someone dies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits with his book in the bedroom, looking troubled by the total lack of explanation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the bedroom stage as the narration specifies the neat resolutions fiction promises.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Toru's growing realization that Kizuki left no dramatic speech or parting note.

explainedBy: Toru stands slumped in an empty void, emotionally frozen in time by the sudden, unexplained absence of his friend.

storyboard.claim: Vanishing without an explanation leaves survivors permanently frozen in time with unresolved grief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru stands bowed and motionless in an empty abstract space, stunned into paralysis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the dorm room to an internal void as the narration addresses the psychological aftermath.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visually conveys the arrested development and emotional freezing that survivor's guilt inflicts.

explainedBy: Toru remains slumped as the abrupt silence of Kizuki's suicide shatters his fundamental understanding of reality.

storyboard.claim: The sudden end of the narrative without conclusion shatters Toru's fundamental understanding of reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru remains slumped in the void with an anxious, distressed expression as his worldview collapses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the abstract void as the paralysis deepens into an existential breakdown.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes that Kizuki's suicide did not just sadden Toru, but destroyed his framework for reality.

explainedBy: Toru stands on one side of the room looking across at the grave marker, visualizing his belief that life and death were separate.

storyboard.claim: Toru previously believed life and death were completely separate domains on opposite sides of existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru stands on one side of a wide room, looking across at a grave marker on the other side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from emotional shock to Toru's philosophical reflection on life and death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages Toru's naive original mental model by physically separating the living youth from the grave marker.

explainedBy: Toru slumps in fear beside the grave marker, realizing that death is already present inside life.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's suicide forces Toru to realize that death is not distant, but already present inside everyday life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru slumps with a frightened expression right beside the grave marker, confronting death's proximity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the room stage, collapsing the distance between Toru and the grave marker.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the collapse of Toru's philosophical boundary between life and death.

explainedBy: Toru sits sorrowfully at a police desk holding his statement papers, seeing death woven into everyday reality.

storyboard.claim: Death is woven into ordinary objects, including the police paperwork and pool balls Toru encounters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits alone at a desk in the police station holding the statement notes, bowed in grief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Anchors the philosophical realization into Toru's concrete memory of giving a police statement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the abstract concept of death's omnipresence to the physical ordeal of the police station.

explainedBy: Kizuki stands with an expressionless, detached gaze, embodying the premeditated mechanics and absolute silence of his suicide.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's suicide was defined by calculated mechanical premeditation and eerie absolute silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki stands motionless in a dim room with a blank, detached expression.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts focus from Toru's mourning to the chilling reality of Kizuki's final actions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Portrays Kizuki's emotional numbness during his meticulously planned suicide.

explainedBy: Kizuki walks out with a detached face, leaving Toru slumped in sorrow behind him in an act of abandonment.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's suicide can be seen as an act of profound cruelty that essentially abandons Toru.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki turns and walks away with a blank face, while Toru slumps in sorrow behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly stages the host's argument that Kizuki's silence constituted brutal abandonment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the psychological abandonment literal by showing Kizuki walking away and deserting his friend.

explainedBy: Toru sits isolated in an interrogation room, bearing the crushing burden of facing the police alone as the last witness.

storyboard.claim: Toru was left to face police interrogation alone, bearing the crushing weight of being the last person to see Kizuki alive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits alone at an interrogation table in a stark room, bowed under an unbearable emotional burden.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the aftermath of Kizuki's departure into the lonely reality of the interrogation room.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the extreme vulnerability and isolation of a seventeen-year-old facing police inquiries.

explainedBy: Naoko and Toru stand slumped together in mutual sorrow, left without a single word of comfort from Kizuki.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki left neither Toru nor Naoko a single word of comfort to help them carry the burden of his death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Naoko and Toru stand side by side, both slumped with sorrowful faces in shared desolation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings Naoko into the frame alongside Toru to illustrate the shared trauma inflicted on both survivors.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals that Kizuki's silence left both of his closest companions equally shattered.

explainedBy: Kizuki stands slumped and anxious, framed as the source of immense collateral damage rather than deliberate malice.

storyboard.claim: The host pushes back against malice, interpreting the survivors' suffering as immense unintended collateral damage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki stands bowed and troubled in an abstract space, struggling under his own unseen agony.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts perspective from the survivors' grief back to Kizuki's internal torment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Humanizes Kizuki by showing him distressed and drowning rather than coldly vengeful.

explainedBy: Kizuki runs in panic, illustrating his suicide as a desperate flight from an unbearable toll.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's death was a desperate escape from an emotional toll he felt incapable of paying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki runs across an abstract void with an expression of terror, fleeing an unseen pressure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the notion of deliberate cruelty with the reality of panic and frantic flight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts suicide as a panicked reaction to overwhelming psychological pressure.

explainedBy: Naoko and Kizuki stand together on an isolated shore smiling innocently, representing their fused childhood on a deserted island.

storyboard.claim: Naoko and Kizuki grew up emotionally fused and isolated from the world, like children on a deserted island.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Naoko and Kizuki stand together on a sunny, peaceful shore, smiling with youthful innocence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens Naoko's backstory to explain the psychological genesis of Kizuki's fragility.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the beautiful but dangerous codependency of their shared childhood.

explainedBy: Kizuki stands slumped and anxious at the water's edge, paralyzed by the emotional toll required to enter adult society.

storyboard.claim: Leaving childhood isolation to enter adult society demands paying a painful toll of individuation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki stands alone at the edge of the shore, slumped and worried as the outside world encroaches.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Disrupts the childhood sanctuary of the shore with the harsh demands of adulthood.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Kizuki's solitary terror when confronted with the pain of growing up.

explainedBy: Kizuki presents a bright, charismatic smile beside a mask, hiding his profound weakness and inability to handle worldly friction.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki projected effortless charm on the surface while desperately hiding his inability to handle reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki poses with an easy, charming smile beside the mask icon in an abstract space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how Kizuki managed to mask his internal collapse from his peers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask explicitly identifies Kizuki's charismatic exterior as a false front concealing weakness.

explainedBy: Kizuki runs in terror across the abstract void, staging his suicide as a panicked flight from a system he could not survive.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's suicide was not an attack on Toru, but a panicked exit from a societal system he could not endure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kizuki flees in terror across an empty void, driven by panic rather than malice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Strips away the charismatic facade to reveal the frantic terror beneath it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes his suicide definitively as an act of terrified escape rather than retribution.

explainedBy: Toru and Naoko stand slumped together in sorrow, the unintended collateral casualties of Kizuki's panicked escape.

storyboard.claim: Toru and Naoko were the tragic collateral casualties of Kizuki's exit, not his intended targets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru and Naoko stand side by side in an abstract void, both bowed down in deep mourning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns from Kizuki's internal panic to the two survivors left in his wake.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes that both Toru and Naoko were struck down by the same collateral shock wave.

explainedBy: Toru slumps with an anxious face while Kizuki's spectral figure stands detached behind him, illustrating how his death infects the living.

storyboard.claim: Kizuki's death does not end his presence; it infects Toru and Naoko with an active, parasitic co-presence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru slumps anxiously in the foreground while Kizuki stands motionlessly behind him like a phantom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from passive collateral damage to the active, ongoing infection of survivor's guilt.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Kizuki not merely as a memory, but as a phantom presence haunting Toru's thoughts.

explainedBy: Toru walks through a Tokyo street carrying a briefcase, attempting to outrun his grief by leaving Kobe behind.

storyboard.claim: Toru tries to escape the geography of his grief by moving from Kobe to a university dorm in Tokyo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru walks resolutely down a Tokyo street carrying a briefcase, determined to start fresh.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from internal haunting to Toru's physical migration to Tokyo.
storyboard.addedInformation: The briefcase and walking stance give tangible form to Toru's attempt at geographic flight.

explainedBy: Toru sits mournfully in his new Tokyo dorm room with Kizuki's silent phantom still beside him, showing that grief cannot be outrun.

storyboard.claim: Changing cities fails to dispel grief; Toru carries Kizuki's ghost straight into his Tokyo room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits with a sorrowful expression in his dorm room, while Kizuki's phantom looms silently behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the futility of geographic escape as the ghost reappears inside Toru's new room.
storyboard.addedInformation: Proves that Toru's survivor guilt is an internal companion that travels everywhere with him.

explainedBy: Toru walks alone through the street beside the city icon, carrying his silent private tragedy into noisy late-1960s Tokyo.

storyboard.claim: Toru brings his intimate, agonizing private tragedy directly into the bustling metropolis of Tokyo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru walks slowly down an urban street beside the city icon, isolated by his silent grief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the dramatic contrast between Toru's quiet mourning and Tokyo's urban roar.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts Toru's internal sorrow with the indifferent magnitude of the surrounding city.

explainedBy: Toru walks detached through the street, surrounded by the performative chaos of the late-1960s student movement.

storyboard.claim: Late 1960s Tokyo was gripped by the loud, performative chaos of the Zenkyoto student movement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru walks through a crowded street with an aloof, blank expression as political agitation brews.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies the historical nature of Tokyo's chaos: radical student activism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Toru's numbness and emotional disconnection from the surrounding political excitement.

explainedBy: The war icon frames the student rebellion, where youth barricaded campuses and clashed violently with riot police.

storyboard.claim: Student protests barricaded campuses, clashed with riot police, and protested the Vietnam War across Japan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The war icon stands framed over a tumultuous street setting, evoking clashes between students and riot police.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates the political backdrop to its violent physical peak of campus barricades.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the militant collective atmosphere contrasting with Toru's solitary experience.

explainedBy: Toru sits quietly at a desk in a university lecture hall holding a book, listening to a lecture on Euripides' tragedy Electra.

storyboard.claim: Toru sits quietly in a university lecture hall as his professor lectures on Euripides' Greek tragedy Electra.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits at a wooden desk in a quiet classroom holding a literature book, listening attentively.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows from nationwide political riots into the quiet order of Toru's literature class.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Toru seeking refuge in classical literature away from the campus violence.

callout.text: TRAPPED BY GHOSTS OF THE PAST

explainedBy: Toru sits holding his book with a sorrowful expression, struck by how Electra portrays characters trapped by ghosts.

storyboard.claim: Euripides' Electra depicts characters trapped by grief and haunted by ghosts, mirroring Toru's state.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits at his desk holding the book, his expression shadowed with sorrowful recognition.
storyboard.onScreenText: TRAPPED BY GHOSTS OF THE PAST
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the classroom scene as the theme of the Greek play reflects Toru's personal dilemma.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Toru realizing that his private agony has been chronicled for thousands of years in tragedy.

explainedBy: Toru looks up in surprise from his book as radical students suddenly bang the lecture hall doors open.

storyboard.claim: The tragedy is a perfect mirror for Toru's grief, shattered when the lecture hall doors suddenly bang open.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru looks up with a startled expression from his book as the classroom doors slam open.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the literature class to the abrupt, violent moment of outside disruption.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the sudden shock of external political noise breaking into Toru's quiet reflection.

explainedBy: The notes icon displays the crude political handbills screaming slogans as helmeted students hijack the class.

storyboard.claim: Helmeted student militants hijack the class, distributing poorly mimeographed leaflets demanding political revolt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sheet of notes representing the crude political leaflets dominates the disrupted classroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Focuses on the militant propaganda leaflets thrust upon the interrupted lecture hall.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the rigid, ideological slogan-chanting of the intruding student activists.

explainedBy: Toru sits at his desk watching with quiet detachment as the professor picks up his cane and limps out of the room.

storyboard.claim: The professor refuses to argue with the students, picking up his cane and limping quietly out of the hall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru sits composed at his desk in the classroom, watching the quiet departure of the professor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the quiet resolution of the disruption: the professor yielding the room to shouting protesters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the professor's dignified, silent withdrawal with the students' empty slogans.

explainedBy: Toru remains seated calmly at his desk, his quiet detachment offering a profound lesson in emotional perspective.

storyboard.claim: Toru's quiet detachment in the face of campus disruption provides a profound lesson in perspective.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru remains seated alone at his desk, observant and utterly unswayed by the surrounding political storm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots focus onto Toru's psychological perspective after the room is overtaken by protesters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights Toru's maturity and perspective compared to the hollow posturing of the militants.

explainedBy: Toru stands slumped in overwhelming mourning, breathing the daily dust of death after his best friend's suicide.

storyboard.claim: Carrying the soul-crushing tragedy of a friend's suicide makes mass political outrage feel completely trivial.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru stands alone and slumped in an abstract void, suffocated by the daily reality of death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the classroom to Toru's internal mourning, explaining why politics cannot penetrate his mind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Conveys the sheer weight of personal bereavement that renders public ideological battles meaningless.

explainedBy: Toru stands detached beside a mask, viewing the sweeping political statements and outrage as merely a game of dress-up.

storyboard.claim: Grand political posturing and societal outrage look like a shallow game of dress-up to a survivor of real tragedy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru stands aloof in an abstract space beside the mask icon, unimpressed by theatrical anger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Directly delivers the hosts' critique of student politics as hollow theatrical posturing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask underscores Toru's realization that the student protesters are merely adopting dramatic poses.

explainedBy: Toru stands slumped in complete defeat, his private grief rendering all grand talk of dismantling society totally hollow.

storyboard.claim: Grand rhetoric about dismantling society feels completely hollow when one's own personal universe has already collapsed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Toru stands slumped in deep sorrow in a stark abstract void, bearing the collapse of his personal world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the sequence comparing campus politics with intimate loss, declaring private grief absolute.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the ultimate primacy of personal grief over public ideological rhetoric.
